what: Video and photo cells are redrawn on a single transparent WebGL plane over the screen — when a cell’s top edge reaches 99% of the screen height, a circle rippling in six directions spreads from the center over .98s power1.inOut and the picture blooms in (with a refracting wave nearby ahead of it). Hovering the cursor makes the plane bulge toward that spot (peak .12 · radius .8), the area around it stretches like a lens (.05) and small ripples rise — entering follows 1−e^(−6dt) and the pointed spot follows 1−e^(−2dt). It is clipped by an ancestor box that hides overflow, and follows the ancestor’s transparency and hiding. fx:hide·fx:show { dur } Fold and unfold with

options.bulge: Bulge toward the cursor (ratio to cell size), default .12
options.[data-fx-part=source]: Source to draw (if none, the first canvas·video·img in the cell)

from.where: index.html Hero video slot · detail.html video · scene slot — original Media(o9Lw-oxa): reveal F = 850×1.15ms power1.inOut, visibility threshold I .99, hover lens L .75 · R .05 · ripple z .25, vertex swell B .12 · radius V .8, hover damping H 6 · pointed spot U 2, overflow-hidden ancestor · clip-path inset cropping

note: The original’s portal effect (a transition where one cell gets pulled toward another on scroll) was left out. The original uses three WebGPU·TSL — the same values were rewritten in GLSL. There is one plate per page, so even with several cells there is only one WebGL context
